newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong securities regulator reprimands Crosby.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong securities regulator reprimands Crosby.

text.p: Hong Kong's securities regulator said on Friday it has publicly reprimanded Crosby Capital Markets (Asia) Ltd in connection with a placement of Giordano International Ltd shares.
The Securities and Futures Commission said an inquiry revealed that Crosby placed 191,526,481 shares in Giordano held by the clothing retailer's founder, Jimmy Lai Chee Ying.

The trade went through on the same day that Giordano announced "there was currently no definite proposal for such placing," and that Lai had not sought Crosby's consent for disposal of his shares, the regulator said.

"The SFC is of the view that a person reading the announcement would reasonably infer that Mr. Lai would not, at least not on the very same day of the announcement, dispose of his shares in Giordano," the regulator said in a statement.
The SFC also criticised Crosby for failing to inform the market of the impending trade, or correct the perception created by the announcement.
"(Crosby) failed in its duty to act in the best interest of the integrity of the market and had, in so doing, prejudiced the interests of members of the investing public," the SFC said.

The trade represented a 27-percent stake in Giordano, which had 708,078,000 shares outstanding at the end of the 1995 calendar year. Lai, who now owns the successful newspaper Apple Daily sold his last remaining Giordano shares at HK$7.60 each, or HK$1.54 billion.

Michael Wu, acting chairman of the SFC, said the regulator is committed to upholding the integrity of the Hong Kong market and takes a serious view of the need for registered intermediaries to act in the best interest of the market while servicing their clients.

"We expect intermediaries to contribute actively towards a fair and orderly market and to conduct their business in a manner which ensures that the market is not misled by carefully crafted announcements intended to create an impression inconsistent with the true intentions of the players," Wu said.
"The investing public has the right to rely on the good faith of announcements made by listed companies at face value."

In a statement, Crosby said: "At the time of Giordano's statement on behalf of Mr Lai, (Crosby) was of the impression that there was no placement forthcoming and accepted this information in good faith. (Crosby) believed at the time it was acting appropriately. (Crosby) subsequently co-operated fully with the SFC."
